titre_page: How to make a brick breaker game in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Make a brick breaker game in Yop2D with no code: a paddle you move with your finger, invisible walls, a bouncing ball, bricks to break, score and lives with nodes.
h1: How to make a brick breaker game?
carte: Paddle moved by finger, bouncing ball, bricks to break, score and lives.
etapes: {{modifier_propriete}} (paddle, y = 1700) → {{garder_dans_ecran}}, with the behavior « Dragged with a finger ».
Surround the screen with invisible walls
Four {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}}s: left_wall, right_wall, top_wall and bottom_wall.
Bounce on the walls and the paddle
blocs: In a brick breaker, a **ball** bounces off walls and off a **paddle** you move with your finger, and breaks **bricks**. Here the ball moves thanks to two variables, **vx** (its speed to the right) and **vy** (its speed downward). When it touches a wall, we simply give it another number.
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **paddle**, at the bottom of the screen (for example 208 x 48 px, around y = 1700);
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **ball**, in the middle of the screen (for example 44 x 44 px);
bricks: {{lang:obj_prefix_image}}s at the top of the screen (for example 128 x 64 px, 8 per row);
two {{lang:obj_prefix_texte}} objects: **scoreText** (text « Score: 0 ») and **livesText** (text « Lives: 3 »), at the top of the screen.

This guide is written for a **1080 x 1920 portrait** game. The images come from the free **Puzzle (brick breaker)** pack (Kenney, free to use, CC0). Download it in the Yop2D **Library**, tab **Packs to download**: you will find **paddleBlu** (paddle), **ballBlue** (ball) and **element_blue_rectangle_glossy** (brick, in blue, green, red, yellow, purple and grey). You can also use your own drawings.
Select a brick. In the inspector, field **{{lang:insp_label_tag}}**, type **brick**. Do the same for every brick.
In the left panel, open the **{{lang:panneau_ress_variables}}** section and create five variables, all with scope **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}** and type **{{lang:var_type_entier}}**:
**bricks**: the **number of bricks** in your game (for example **24**). It tells you when everything is broken;
**vx** and **vy**: starting value **0**. This is the ball's speed, set when the game starts.
One brick more or less? Just change the starting value of **bricks**. If the number is too big, you never win; if it is too small, you win too early.
The ball bounces off walls you cannot see: four **{{lang:obj_prefix_zone}}s** placed around the screen. A zone is invisible during the game, but the ball can touch it.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **left_wall**: X = `-300`, Y = `-400`, width `300`, height `2800`.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **right_wall**: X = `1080`, Y = `-400`, width `300`, height `2800`.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **top_wall**: X = `-300`, Y = `-300`, width `1680`, height `300`.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **bottom_wall**: X = `-300`, Y = `1920`, width `1680`, height `300`.
The walls are thick on purpose: a fast ball cannot go through them. The first three send the ball back; **bottom_wall** is used to lose a life.
Step 3: the paddle follows your finger
Select **paddle**, touch **⚙ Comportement de l'objet** and choose **Dragged with a finger**: the player takes it and moves it.
Open the scene's **{{lang:titre_blueprint}}** and add the **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]** event.
Link the three nodes in order.

**Why these two nodes?** « Dragged with a finger » lets the paddle move in every direction. On every frame, we put it back at the same height and keep it from leaving the screen: it only moves left and right.
Add the **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event, then two **[[modifier_variable]]** nodes one after the other: variable **vx**, value `6`, then variable **vy**, value `-9`.
In the settings window of **[[pousser]]**, touch the **🔗** button next to **Add X**, choose **[[valeur_variable]]**, then choose the variable **vx** in the green node that appears.
Do the same for **Add Y** with the variable **vy**.
Link each event to its nodes and run the game: the ball goes up and to the right, then leaves the screen.
**A green node** gives a value to a setting, without typing anything. Here, **[[valeur_variable]]** tells **[[pousser]]**: « move by **vx** to the right and by **vy** downward, on every frame ».
**Negative = up.** In Yop2D, Y grows toward the bottom of the screen: **vy = -9** sends the ball upward.
Each wall gives the ball a new number. Add three **[[NoeudEventCollisionAB]]** events (**Object A** = **ball**):
**Object B** = **left_wall** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**, value `6` (the ball goes back to the right).
**Object B** = **right_wall** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**, value `-6` (the ball goes back to the left).
**Object B** = **top_wall** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vy**, value `9` (the ball goes back down).
Add **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vy**, value `-9` (the ball goes back up).
Add a second **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**. Touch **🔗** next to the value, choose **[[valeur_hasard]]**, then set **From** = `-6` and **To** = `6`.
On every bounce on the paddle, the ball leaves in a **random direction**: the game is never the same twice.
Add **[[detruire_objet]]** and choose **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}** as the target: it is the brick the ball has just touched.

Add **[[condition]]** `=vy < 0` (« the ball is going up »). Output **{{lang:port_vrai}}** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vy**, value `9`. Output **{{lang:port_faux}}** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vy**, value `-9`.
From the **[[lang:port_ensuite]]** output of the condition, add **[[ajouter_variable]]**: variable **score**, **{{lang:ajouter_variable.valeur}} = 10**.
**Why `=vy < 0`?** If **vy** is smaller than 0, the ball is going up: after breaking the brick, it goes down. Otherwise it is going down, and it goes back up.
**The = sign at the beginning of the text** tells Yop2D to **calculate** the text instead of writing it as it is (see the guide [Collect coins and count points](guide:pieces-score)).

On the **{{lang:port_vrai}}** output: **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `0`, **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `0` (the ball stops), then **[[toast]]** with the message **You win!**, then **[[attendre]]** 2 seconds, then **[[recommencer_scene]]**.
[[recommencer_scene]] puts the objects back in place and the **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}** variables back to their starting value: the game restarts with 3 lives, 0 points and all the bricks.
When the ball touches **bottom_wall** (under the screen), the player loses a life.

Output **{{lang:port_vrai}}** (no lives left): **[[deplacer]]** the **ball** to X = `518`, Y = `1000`, **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `0`, **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `0` (the ball is put back in the middle and stops), then **[[toast]]** « Game over! », **[[attendre]]** 2 seconds, **[[recommencer_scene]]**.
Output **{{lang:port_faux}}** (lives left): **[[deplacer]]** the **ball** to X = `518`, Y = `1000`, then **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `-9`, then **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `6`.

**Why stop the ball before waiting?** During the 2 seconds of waiting, the game keeps running. If the ball stayed below the screen, it would cost a life on every frame, and the lives counter would drop very low. Put back in the middle and motionless, it no longer causes trouble.
**Sounds:** add **[[jouer_son]]** after **[[detruire_objet]]** (a « clack » when a brick breaks) and in the paddle event.
**Different colors:** give the same tag **brick** to all the bricks, whatever their color: a single setup is enough.
**A faster ball:** change the numbers `6`, `-6`, `9` and `-9` everywhere (for example `8`, `-8`, `12` and `-12`).
**Sparks:** add an **[[effet_particules]]** when a brick breaks (see the guide [Particles and effects](guide:particules-effets)).

**The ball doesn't move:** check that **vx** and **vy** change at the start, and that **[[pousser]]** is linked to the green **[[valeur_variable]]** nodes (touch **Add X**: the line must show the green wire).

**The ball goes through a wall or the bricks:** check the names (**ball**, **paddle**, **left_wall**…) and the tag **brick**, spelled the same everywhere (no capital letter). If the ball is very fast, make the bricks a little bigger or slow the ball down.
**The paddle goes up or down:** the **[[modifier_propriete]]** node must be linked to **{{NoeudEventChaqueImage}}**, with **Property** = `y`.
**You win too early or never:** the variable **bricks** must be exactly the number of bricks in the game.
**To compare**, open the test project (its nodes are sorted by section, with frames and sticky notes that explain each part).
